text:
Dana: Heads-up  Cobalt Analytics wants a Private POC today. They prefer VPC peering into our control plane and will egress via their firewall NAT. Need a compact handoff I can send to their cloud eng.

Ibrahim: Quick list to ask for: full customer CIDRs, RTB IDs they'll update, chosen AZs/subnet IDs for peering, and any NAT EIP(s) for egress allowlist. Also confirm peering vs PrivateLink preference.

Dana: They sent 10.130.0.0/16 (apps) + 10.131.32.0/19 (dc). Peering for POC.

Riley: Minimal routing we require: their RTB -> create route to Redwood control CIDR 10.230.0.0/16 via pcx-XXXXX. Our RTB -> create route to their app CIDR 10.130.0.0/16 via pcx-XXXXX. Ensure no overlapping prefixes and enable DNS resolution on peering.

Ibrahim: Pasteable AWS CLI for them (customer side):
```bash
aws ec2 create-route --route-table-id rtb-cust123 --destination-cidr-block 10.230.0.0/16 --vpc-peering-connection-id pcx-0a1b2c
```
Our side (Redwood):
```bash
aws ec2 create-route --route-table-id rtb-rwd456 --destination-cidr-block 10.130.0.0/16 --vpc-peering-connection-id pcx-0a1b2c
aws ec2 modify-vpc-peering-connection-options --vpc-peering-connection-id pcx-0a1b2c --accepter-peering-connection-options AllowDnsResolutionFromRemoteVpc=true --requester-peering-connection-options AllowDnsResolutionFromRemoteVpc=true
```
Replace IDs.

Riley: DNS options: fastest for POC = peering + Route53 resolver (customer creates outbound rule forwarding our private zone queries to our resolver IPs). PrivateLink option: they create interface endpoints per AZ, use SGs and endpoint DNS; avoids RTB edits but slower to provision.

sec-bot: Security checklist to paste into questionnaire: "Redwood requires VPC peering or PrivateLink for Private POCs. Routes must explicitly target Redwood control plane CIDR 10.230.0.0/16. Management plane: TCP/443 from peered CIDRs or specified ENI IPs. No propagation of default route (0.0.0.0/0) into peered tables. TLS 1.2+, mutual TLS recommended for production. Provide NAT EIP(s) if using centralized egress for outbound allowlisting."

Dana: They asked about least-privilege for management plane. Can we provide ENI IPs?

Riley: Yes, we can provide control-plane ENI IP addresses once the peering is created and accepted; for POC we accept peered CIDR temporarily but create a ticket to tighten to ENIs before production.

Ibrahim: If they'd like automation: they can create an assume-role in their account allowing us to accept the peering via CI. Provide role ARN and duration. Otherwise they accept manually.

deploy-bot: Note: staging and automated deploys will pause until peering is active. Create support ticket to collect RTB IDs, NAT EIPs, resolver IPs, and decision (peering|privatelink).

Dana: Perfect  I'll send this to Cobalt's cloud eng and ask for RTB IDs + NAT EIPs and whether they want us to accept via assume-role. Will update the thread when they reply. :thumbsup:
